summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 19th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with only mild nausea, which was managed with lorazepam and prochlorperazine. Methotrexate levels were monitored daily, declining to 0.14 uM by discharge, allowing safe transition home. Leucovorin rescue and sodium bicarbonate were administered as scheduled to support methotrexate clearance. Aspirin was held during admission and restarted at discharge, with heparin used for DVT prophylaxis. Liver enzymes showed mild, expected elevation, and her hemoglobin remained stable. She reported ongoing chronic right foot pain, managed with gabapentin and PRN oxycodone, and denied depressive symptoms, remaining on citalopram. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete three days of leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate and to continue alternating methotrexate and rituximab therapy.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase or lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
